extractions.value: We also had the opportunity to evaluate the patient during a respiratory crisis challenged by a forced maneuver of full inhalation and exhalation, as necessary to perform spirometry. Immediately after the maneuver, the patient became intensely agitated, due to severe respiratory constraint and chest pain. Physical auscultation revealed absence of lung sounds. A very high-pitched noise, such as a stridor, could be heard at some distance. Apart from tachycardia, no signs of paroxysmal autonomic dysfunction, such as diaphoresis and hyperpyrexia, were observed. Blood pressure values were normal. Low-flow oxygen was administered. The EMG recordings showed increased activity of the sternocleidomastoid and, to a greater extent, of the abdominal muscles, with an interferential pattern. Polygraphic recording showed a prolonged apnea with persisting thoracic and abdominal movements, which occurred out of phase.

This is a Letter to the Editor reporting instrumental respiratory monitoring in a 55-year-old woman with SPS. A detailed clinical history was previously reported in reference [5]. The paper focuses on respiratory crises: baseline stiffness of abdominal and thoracic paraspinal muscles with trunk hyperextension; continuous motor unit activity on EMG; a respiratory crisis triggered by forced inhalation/exhalation with stridor, prolonged apnea, out-of-phase thoracoabdominal movements, and acute respiratory acidosis; resolution with intranasal midazolam. The patient had transient paroxysmal hypertension responsive to benzodiazepines.
